#3129. Sketchy suggestion of ceramic iPhone 20 Pro

A sketchy rumor is doing the rounds suggesting that Apple is working on a ceramic edition of the iPhone 20 Pro.

There are no details, and while one concept image shows a ceramic back, this seems a rather unlikely possibility …

Fixed Focus Digital is one of those pointing to the possibility, stating that they have seen ceramic components for next year’s flagship iPhone. An image has also been shared by Tech Overwatch, which is very clearly a render, simply imagining what it might look like.

Details are very vague, so it’s possible that the whole thing is a misunderstanding based on Apple’s Ceramic Shield protection for the display and glass back, as seen on the iPhone Air.

Given that the iPhone 20 Pro will itself be a very premium device and involve a completely new production line setup, it seems rather unlikely Apple would want to either launch a super-premium version or experiment with two different versions at the same time. What are your own thoughts? Please share in the comments.

#3128. Community-Focused Academic Brings AI Tools to Colorado Farmers

This senior member’s chatbot helps them start agritourism businesses

Willie Jones covers transportation for IEEE Spectrum and the history of technology for The Institute.

Alice Dong has created an AI chatbot website that helps Colorado farmers plan and operate agribusinesses that draw visitors to their properties.

Many farmers and ranchers in eastern Colorado are curious about artificial intelligence, but they don’t have a local tech-savvy person to show them how to use it. Xue “Alice” Dong has made that her job.

Dong, an IEEE senior member, is an extension regional specialist with the Colorado State University Extension, CSU’s outreach arm. She works in Logan County and serves a 10-county farming area in Colorado’s northeast corner. Her job is to turn university research into practical help for the people who live there.

Xue “Alice” Dong Employer Colorado State University Extension in Logan CountyTitle Extension regional specialistMember grade Senior memberAlma maters Inner Mongolia Normal University, in Hohhot; Beijing Normal University; State University of New York College of Environmental Science and Forestry, in Syracuse; Colorado State University Global

Colorado State University Extension in Logan County

Inner Mongolia Normal University, in Hohhot; Beijing Normal University; State University of New York College of Environmental Science and Forestry, in Syracuse; Colorado State University Global

She built the AI-Powered Agritourism Chatbot (AgriTourismAI.com), which helps farmers and ranchers launch and run “agritourism” businesses. Agritourism is when farmers open their property to visitors for fun, education, or shopping events. Familiar examples include pick-your-own fruit orchards, lessons on how to grow vegetables, and sales of handmade products.

Dong also teaches workshops where she shows farmers and ranchers how they can use AI tools to help grow and manage their business.

She says she sees herself as a link between the university and the countryside.

“We [extension specialists] act as a bridge,” she says. “We bridge our campus to the rural communities we serve.”

Many farmers and ranchers are older, and they typically have no technical training. Often their children and grandchildren have left the farm to work in a city or otherwise aren’t around to teach them about new tools. Without help, the benefits of AI could pass the farmers by. Dong’s workshops give them a way in.

Dong was named a finalist in the 2026 GenAI for Good Challenge for her AgriPivot AI Agent. The challenge was organized by IEEE Humanitarian Technologies and theU.N.’s International Telecommunication Union, and her project was selected from 318 teams across 79 countries. She also won the 2026 Award for Innovation from the National Extension Technology Community (NETC), and both the 2025 national and Western regional Educational Technology Awards from the National Association of Community Development Extension Professionals (NACDEP).

She has secured seven competitive grants totaling more than US $250,000 as principal investigator or co-principal investigator, including funding supported by the Department of Agriculture’s National Institute of Food and Agriculture.

Dong was born in Beijing. Both her parents are doctors.

As a child, she liked drawing new and inventive things. Sketching, she says, lets her picture solutions to problems in her head and put them on paper as practical designs.

That habit grew into a way of relating to her surroundings.

“I’ve always had a passion to create something tangible that can solve problems in the real world,” she says.

She doesn’t credit a single mentor for the direction her life has taken. Instead, she says all her teachers helped lay the groundwork for her career.

She attended the Inner Mongolia Normal University, in Hohhot, an institution that trains teachers. She earned two bachelor’s degrees there in 2013—one in geographical science and one in education.

She then earned a master’s degree in curriculum and instruction from Beijing Normal University in 2016.

That year, she moved to the United States to continue her graduate studies at the State University of New York College of Environmental Science and Forestry, in Syracuse. She earned a master’s degree in environmental biology in 2020.

After earning her second master’s degree, she joined Paul Smith’s College, in Paul Smiths, N.Y., as an education and outreach coordinator.

She managed several national watershed projects to protect rivers, lakes, and aquifers. Watersheds are areas of land from which water drains into bodies of water.

She also undertook invasive-species-prevention projects, wrote grants to secure project funding, and designed two educational websites and several outreach publications. One website, Maintain the Chain, helps lake residents, boaters, and visitors from around the world keep invasive species out of the Fulton Chain of Lakes in New York’s Adirondack Park.

In 2022, she joined Stewards of the Coast and Redwoods as program manager. The nonprofit, based in Guerneville, Calif., works with California State Parks to protect, restore, and educate the public about the parks along Sonoma County’s coast and the Russian River area. The region is known for its redwood forests, wineries, and resort towns.

She left in 2023 to join the CSU Extension as a regional specialist, a title she still holds.

Her employer is part of the Cooperative Extension System, a nationwide network run by land-grant universities, schools founded with federal grants to teach farming and other practical subjects. Extension faculty and staff share what researchers at their universities learn with the citizens of those states.

The cooperative system operates on three levels. It is overseen federally by the Department of Agriculture’s National Institute of Food and Agriculture, managed statewide through land-grant universities, and delivered locally by county offices and Extension agents across more than 3,000 counties.

The work goes well beyond farming, Dong says, also covering community and economic development, health initiatives, and the 4-H program, which teaches children hands-on skills in agriculture, science, leadership, and citizenship.

Extension faculty members’ performance is judged on their research, teaching, and service to the community, Dong says—similar to the way professors in academia are evaluated. The difference, she says, is the audience: Professors teach students; most extension specialists teach adults, including farmers, ranchers, and community leaders. The setting is different, too. Dong doesn’t commute from the campus to the countryside; she lives and works in it. Her office is in Sterling, a small rural town. But her projects serve the whole state, and many of the people she helps live one to four hours’ drive away. So, most of her work with farmers and ranchers happens by email, phone, and virtual meetings. County fairs, farmers markets, and agricultural events give her chances to meet large groups of them in person.

She can’t just hand Colorado residents research findings and expect them to figure out the information they need, she says.

“We need to translate that research into something more practical, and easier to use, that farmers and ranchers can understand immediately,” she says.

Dong also focuses not on only on whether people use AI, but also on how they use it. In 2026, she and Paul Hill from Utah State University Extension published “From Access to Governance: Generative AI Literacy for Extension Professionals and Small Businesses, and a Governance-Aware Design Framework” in the journal AI. The paper offers a framework for helping Extension professionals and small businesses adopt generative AI responsibly.

In 2025, Dong earned a third master’s degree, in artificial intelligence and machine learning, from CSU Global.

She immediately put those skills to work on agritourism, she says. She built the chatbot in Python, a popular programming language. It answers typed questions, and its user interface looks much like ChatGPT’s, but it works differently. Under the hood, it uses retrieval-augmented generation, a technique that has the AI look up information in a set of trusted documents before it answers. Dong curated that collection from Extension publications, so the chatbot’s answers rest on authoritative sources and are less likely to be made up. She presented the project at NeurIPS 2025 (Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems). The code is openly available on GitHub, so other Extension offices can adapt it.

The bot runs in a web browser rather than as a phone app. Many farmers she works with don’t own a smartphone, Dong says, but nearly all have a computer, tablet, or other gadget that can connect to a website. The bot works on any of them, with no app to download.

Extension specialists “act as a bridge. We bridge our campus to the rural communities we serve.”

Farmers often ask the bot how to attract visitors and how to write a business plan. A farmer thinking about opening a corn maze, for example, can ask how to price admission, what kind of insurance to carry, and which permits to get. The bot also gives advice on managing risk.

One of her test sites was Prairie Ridge Buffalo Ranch, in eastern Colorado. Dong documented how the ranch put AI to work in a peer-reviewed case study, “Revolutionizing Agritourism with AI and Machine Learning: A Case Study of Prairie Ridge Buffalo Ranch in Colorado,” published in 2025 in CABI Tourism Cases.

Surveys and interviews she conducted with other users showed that people find it’s easy to use the bot, learn from it, and act on its advice, she says. She is preparing the full results for publication.

Her work extends beyond agritourism. In 2026, she contributed an AI assistant to Project Pythia, an open-science program funded by the U.S. National Science Foundation and led by the National Center for Atmospheric Research (NCAR). The AI assistant turns raw airport weather report data into plain-language guidance for farmers and other non-technical users, and it tells users when data is missing rather than guessing.

She also teaches workshops on AI tools such as ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini. She has taught her workshop 20 times to more than 200 entrepreneurs and business owners, who came from 32 Colorado counties. In follow-up surveys, 90 percent of participants reported trying at least one new AI task in their business. Some of the workshops take place at a community center run by the Logan County Economic Development Corp., in Sterling. She has also co-hosted the workshops with the Rural Community Assistance Corp., Colorado Startup Week, and Boulder Startup Week. And she occasionally presents them as webinars, so people don’t have to travel.

Her outreach has taught her that many farmers are eager to try new tools, she says. She shows them how simple her chatbot is to use.

She also offers advice to high school students drawn to the field. Extension specialists each have a specialty, such as livestock, natural resources, food systems, or 4-H. Students should pick one based on their passion, she says.

Land-grant universities offer related programs at the bachelor’s and master’s levels. For graduate students, she adds, Extension offers a third career path beyond academia and industry: “You apply advanced skills directly to the communities that need them.”

Dong joined IEEE in 2025 and soon was elevated to senior member. Her professional home is the IEEE Society on Social Implications of Technology. She also serves as vice treasurer of the IEEE Denver Section’s Young Professionals group.

IEEE supports all three parts of her job, she says. For research, she presented “Entrepreneur AI Agent: Empowering Small Businesses and Bridging the Digital Divide through Context-Aware Generative AI” at the 2026 IEEE Global Humanitarian Technology Conference (GHTC). For teaching, she has offered to bring her AI workshop to Denver Section members and local entrepreneurs. For service, she reviews papers for IEEE conferences.

IEEE conferences matter most to her, she says: “Through them, I can present my research and network with other researchers in the field.”

She attended the IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology in Boulder, Colo., in September 2026. The event, she says, opened her eyes to many new projects underway across IEEE.

Still, she says, her work always points back to the farms and ranches of eastern Colorado. Its people are curious, she says, but they can’t make the leap to new technology alone.

“They really need this kind of a bridge,” she says.

Willie Jones is an associate editor at IEEE Spectrum. In addition to editing and planning daily coverage, he manages several of Spectrum's newsletters and contributes regularly to the monthly Big Picture section that appears in the print edition.

#3127. Caterpillar's $78 Billion Backlog, Explained

Caterpillar's order backlog nearly doubled over the past year, yet shares are trading at just 16.5 times forward earnings. See how this $78 billion unfilled order list sets up the industrial giant for long-term sales growth.

By Anders Bylund – Nov 26, 2026 at 1:37PM EST

10 stocks we like better than Caterpillar ›

Looking at Caterpillar's (CAT +0.57%) stock chart lately feels like a market paradox.

On one hand, the heavy-machinery giant is sitting on a staggering, all-time-high $78 billion order backlog -- nearly double the $39.8 billion list it had a year ago. On the other hand, the stock has been cut roughly in half from its 52-week high, leaving shares trading at a modest 16.5 times forward earnings.

So, what gives? First, that $78 billion pile of orders isn't some accounting mirage cooked up by overly optimistic customers.

Artificial intelligence data centers require colossal amounts of electricity, and hyperscalers are snapping up Caterpillar's industrial gas turbines and massive reciprocating engines as fast as the company can build them. Power generation retail sales jumped 75% year over year in the third quarter, and customers are already booking production slots out to 2029 and 2030 just to get in line.

Even better, Caterpillar's momentum isn't trapped in a strict artificial intelligence silo. Construction equipment sales to end users climbed 20% in the third quarter -- marking seven straight quarters of growth -- thanks to major infrastructure projects and commercial builds. Even the mining division is seeing healthy order rates for copper and gold operations.

However, management expects 58% of the current backlog to convert into revenue within the next 12 months.

Rather than a temporary double-ordering boost, Caterpillar is backing the demand with physical capacity expansions. The company plans to nearly triple large reciprocating engine production by 2030 along with a $1 billion manufacturing investment in North Carolina.

For long-term investors, the massive backlog provides multi-year revenue visibility as the capacity constraints gradually ease.

#3125. I Don’t Trust Visual Recordings Anymore. But One Day I Will Again

We will have to label our content to prove its authenticity

Hany Farid is a computer science professor at Dartmouth College, in Hanover, N.H.

In March of this year, a flurry of emails and text messages from a half dozen reporters around the world disrupted my quiet Saturday morning. An Iranian news agency had aired a week-old video of what appeared to be a U.S.-made Tomahawk missile hitting a school. News reports claimed that the strike killed more than 175 people, most of them children. The U.S. president and military denied responsibility. In the age of generative AI and all things deepfake, everyone—including me—was skeptical of the video’s authenticity.

I get this type of request a lot. For the past three decades, I’ve been developing mathematical and computational techniques to analyze and detect manipulation in digital media. Over this time, I think it’s fair to say that I, like most people, have approached visual recordings with a “presumption of authenticity”: If a skeptic claims that a recording is fake, the burden of proof is on them.

In today’s world of generative AI, however, I think we need to shift this stance to a “presumption of fake.” That is, the burden is now on the creator to prove that their content is real. While this new stance may seem unfair to legitimate creators, I think it both reflects reality and points to a future where we will once again be able to trust that most online media is what it appears to be.

Even last March, I was already tilting toward a presumption of fake. My initial response to the reporters was something along the lines of, “I am suspicious of the video because the quality is low, it emerged weeks after the bombing, and it is only being distributed by an Iranian news agency with a less-than-stellar record of accurate reporting.”

Given the potential implications—if the video was indeed real, however, I resigned myself to spending my Saturday morning analyzing it.

I first reasoned that if the Tomahawk missile was digitally added to each frame of the video without taking into consideration the camera motion, we might see a physically implausible missile path. So I aligned the video frames using a stationary background landmark as a reference. In the updated video, the missile did, in fact, move in a nearly linear trajectory. (See the yellow dots in the composite shown below.)

I next asked if the size (in pixels) of the missile in the video was plausible. Under some reasonable assumptions, I estimated that the missile in the video corresponded to a 6-meter Tomahawk at a distance of approximately 100 meters. The distance seemed plausible from the scene and was also consistent with the delay of 0.3 seconds from visible impact to the sound of impact, given that sound travels at 343 meters per second.

A composite photo composed of frames from a video of the Tomahawk strike reveals the missile’s trajectory.Hany Farid; Source: Mehr News

Despite the mounting evidence, though, I struggled to refine my answer for the reporters.

My skepticism was fueled by a recent study I worked on with colleagues at the University of California, Berkeley, that showed how hard it is to distinguish real from fake videos. Observers are now so suspicious of videos in general that they have trouble convincing themselves that a video is real.

But after a few more hours and a few more analyses with the missile video, I finally decided that it was authentic, and I gave the reporters my updated view.

This analysis marked a turning point for me. I realized I was just like the participants in our study: The lack of artifacts was not enough to readily convince me a video is real. I had flipped from a presumption of real to a presumption of fake.

When the visual record is no longer reliable, what can we do?

The types of forensic analyses that I routinely perform do not currently operate at internet scale and speed. But provenance signals can. These signals include content credentials and watermarks that are inserted or embedded at the time of creation or recording.

Credentials that follow the C2PA standard, for example, attach a cryptographically signed manifest to a photo or video at the moment of capture; this metadata records the device, the time and location of the recording, and any subsequent edits. Because the manifest is signed, any tampering with either the content or its history can be detected later by machine. Watermarks, like Google’s SynthID, embed an imperceptible signal directly into the pixels or audio samples that identifies the content’s origin.

Apple recently took these ideas a step further. On some of its newest iPhones, the camera sensor can cryptographically sign the raw pixel data as it’s captured. That signed data is then developed into a reference image saved alongside the normal, editable photo. Anyone can then compare the two and see exactly what, if anything, was changed.

These provenance signals are often criticized as being only a partial solution or vulnerable to attack. This is true if we think of them as mechanisms for catching bad actors. But that’s not what they’re supposed to do. Their purpose is to let good actors prove that their audiovisual recording is what it claims to be.

Provenance signals thus need not be adversary-proof. Instead, these signals are part of a new reality in which consumers, journalists, and the courts must adapt to a presumption of fakeness. If enough good actors adopt these mechanisms, they can begin to drown out bad actors. In other words, we have to switch from a model of “catch the bad actors” to “empower the good actors.”

This switch from trust to distrust of digital media has expanded to include routine video calls.

In September 2024, for example, Senator Ben Cardin (D-Md.), then chair of the Foreign Relations Committee, received a video meeting request from Dmytro Kuleba, who until a few weeks earlier had been Ukraine’s foreign minister. During the call, Cardin became suspicious when, out of character, Kuleba pressed him on whether the U.S. should allow Ukraine to fire long-range missiles into Russia. Cardin ended the call. Later, the State Department confirmed that Kuleba had never requested the meeting, and the Senate security office warned staff that foreign adversaries, possibly Russian, would likely try similar faked meetings again.

All it takes to conduct this type of impersonation is a face swap or avatar deepfake, along with voice conversion, both of which substitute the speaker’s face and voice for deepfaked versions in real time. These technologies are readily available in commercial products and open-source libraries and run on nothing more powerful than a modern laptop.

This video illustrates the current state of face-swap deepfakes.

Farid’s Company GetReal Shows How Real Deepfake Videos Look Today Your browser does not support the video tag. Firms that verify provenance have to move fast to detect real-time deepfakes. Hany Farid, GetReal

Firms that verify provenance have to move fast to detect real-time deepfakes. Hany Farid, GetReal

Unlike the Tomahawk video, which I could sit with for a morning analyzing frame by frame, a live video call offers no time for human analysis. On the other hand, real-time deepfakes pose new challenges for their creators: A fake video call has to be generated at around 24 frames per second to fool the eye into perceiving realistic motion. As a result, the deepfake-video-call software has to take shortcuts, such as simplifying faces and how they interact with their surroundings, and allowing some drift between audio and video or between video frames. The human eye doesn’t notice the shortcuts, but we can forensically expose them.

Provenance signals should eventually play a role here. Video-calling software could apply the same cryptographic signing to each frame of a live video stream that Apple now applies to still photographs. A face swap necessarily occurs between a speaker’s camera and the videoconferencing software, and so the software could verify in real time whether the frames it’s receiving were signed by a physical camera sensor or whether they were altered in transit. As before, the burden shifts from catching the impersonator to allowing real participants to prove they are who they claim to be.

For the first two decades of the digital revolution, forensic analysis—finding the telltale traces of manipulation—was enough to adjudicate most questions of authenticity. The AI revolution, however, has changed the scale and speed of manipulation beyond what forensics alone can handle. To believe a recording is real now, it must also carry a provenance signal from the point of recording. The two approaches work together, with provenance allowing good actors to be trusted, while forensic analyses root out the bad actors.

Hany Farid is a computer science professor at Dartmouth College, in Hanover, N.H. About 10 years ago, he randomly picked up a book in the library on the federal rules of evidence and was astonished to learn that courts made no distinction between photos from negatives and digital photos, even though the latter can be easily altered. “Digital photography was just getting started,” Farid says. “I realized this was really going to be a huge problem.” Since then digital photo forensics has become the focus of his research. He now frequently testifies in U.S. courts and advises law enforcement agencies. “All that from picking up a book,” he says.

The emerging authentication and provenance systems make a lot of sense for mainstream uses. I get the impression we'll still need forensic analysis for plenty of edge cases, though. People using older hardware or anyone trying to capture evidence in situations where it isn't safe to share clues about the media's origin come to mind.

The Blink Mini 2K+ is an affordable indoor camera with a wired connection that offers high-resolution live-view footage, a built-in LED spotlight and two-way audio. The camera also detects motion, so you can put your mind at ease when away from home. You can arm, disarm or simply check on your house from anywhere using the Blink app or via the Alexa Blink smart home skill on any Echo device. Now at an all-time low price on Amazon.

One of Blink's cheapest deals is this Video Doorbell System, which includes a Sync Module Core for secure footage storage. Blink's doorbell has a two-year battery life, meaning you won't have to worry about hardwiring if you're renting. It also has a 150° head-to-toe view, can automatically send you parcel and person alerts, and helps keep your worries at bay with continuous live view.

Now 66% off, Blink has combined its Outdoor 2k+ and Mini 2k+ into an affordable home security package. You'll score two of each camera for the ultimate protection when you're away from home, and you'll get the Blink Sync Module 2, which allows you to store your footage locally.

Better yet, you'll be able to check in on your home and view footage in 2K clear resolution, even at night and zoom in on all the nooks and crannies around your home. What a win.

If you’re keen to fit out your house with the whole kit and caboodle, Blink has discounted the lot and bundled them up for easy purchasing. With a Mini 2, Blink Doorbell and Sync Module Core, it’s an extensive and inexpensive way to cover the entire home. And to top it off, you'll also receive a 30-day free trial of Blink's subscription plan to try it out. What a win.

Nab a new Wi-Fi router with this limited-time eero 7 deal. With 15% off, this two-pack of Wi-Fi 7 modems can support NBN plans with up to 2.5Gbps speeds and over 120 devices with minimal to no interruptions.

The Echo Dot offers impressive audio quality for a smart speaker. While it's not the cheapest we have seen, this smart speaker comes with voice control via Alexa too, so you can stream your favourite apps, listen to music or the news and schedule reminders.

The latest Echo home display devices have gotten a much-needed glow-up in the Echo Show 8 and the Echo Show 11. Aside from the updated in-cell touch and negative liquid crystal screens, both devices include new front-facing stereo speakers and a custom woofer for room-filling spatial audio. The key difference between the two? The Echo Show 8 has a smaller 8.7-inch display.

With all the same great features as the Echo Show 8 above, if you're after a larger home display screen to connect to your Ring devices, check recipes while cooking or control your smart devices using Alexa, then the 11-inch Echo Show could be the move for you.

The Echo Dot Max features almost 3x the bass of the Echo Dot (5th gen), and its sound can automatically adapt to your space, making it the perfect addition to any smart home or party setup. We gave it a nice 4 stars in our review, namely for its great smart home capabilities and stellar sound.

If you're looking to amplify your home streaming set-up, this Fire TV Cube offers lightning-fast app loading thanks to its octa-core processor — which is 2x more powerful than the Fire TV Stick 4K Max. You can stream more than 350k movies and TV shows with access to all of your favourite streamers and free-to-air channels. While it has been cheaper before, the TV Cube is rarely discounted, so this is still a solid deal.

Elevate your home entertainment experience with the Fire TV Stick 4K Plus. This nifty gadget plugs into any TV's HDMI port and allows you to stream Netflix, Binge, Prime Video and more, all from an Alexa-enabled remote. Note that the Fire TV Stick 4K Plus is a new name for the Fire TV Stick 4K, but they are otherwise identical.

Looking to beef up home security but worried about the cost? The Ring Indoor Camera 2 is now massively discounted. Simply plug it into the nearest wall socket, link it up with the Ring app and you'll have access to sharp 1080p video footage within your home. It even comes with a 30-day free trial of Ring Protect, which allows you to keep old footage on file — though you will have to pay a subscription fee after the trial is up if you want to keep said videos. And this is the second-lowest price it's been on Amazon so far.

Knock a nice 30% off this Pan-Tilt camera, designed specifically for pet owners. With a 169° tilt and 360° pan angles, you can monitor every nook and cranny of your home when you're away, and make sure Fido and Tiger don't get up to mischief. Available in both black and white colourways at this all-time low price.

Give your home a doorbell and gain some peace of mind with the newest Ring Video Doorbell (Battery). As the name suggests, it has a built-in rechargeable battery, so you don't need an electrician to install it. That said, you do have the option of wiring it into your home's electrical system if you'd prefer. Provides 24/7 video capture in crystal-clear Retinal 2K and offers 6x zoom. Do note that this discount is exclusive to the Speckled Grey colourway.

Apartment dwellers, rejoice! If you live in a building with an eligible system, Ring's Intercom device can answer the door for packages or people when you're not home, taking the stress off any missed deliveries. Better yet, this deal comes with an Indoor Camera so you can monitor anyone inside (or outside) your home.

The Pixel 10 Pro may not be Google's latest flagship, but it's still a fantastic buy for anyone after a reliable Android phone at a great price. Expect the clean Pixel software experience, excellent camera performance and powerful AI features that Google's phones are known for. With a 20,000mAh capacity and 20W power delivery, this option from Vrurc is ideal for those who need to extend their phone's battery life well beyond what it's typically capable of, and who don't want to lug around a bulky bank.

This power bank can charge at up to 145W, and has dual USB-C ports, plus a USB-A. You can charge multiple devices at once, including your laptop and phone at the same time.

If you're an Apple user and you want to keep tabs on your luggage, your pet, your house keys or anything else, AirTags are your best bet. These are the original ones, with the 4-pack now down to an all-time low price, just AU$2 off the lowest AU$129 we saw in October.

While we've not reviewed this 75% mechanical gaming keyboard ourselves, reviews from other reputable sources across the web are largely glowing, praising its construction quality, performance and low price. It's even available with two switch styles and a range of six colours.

Logitech's Pebble 2 mouse and keyboard combo is a great option for Mac users, offering a blend of style and practicality at an affordable price. These devices connect via a Bluetooth dongle and feature a sleek, ultra-slim design, perfect for portability.

While this mini home projector has been discounted to this price before on Amazon, it's still a great deal. Our friends at TechRadar gave its predecessor 4.5 stars in their review, so we're confident the next-gen is just as super.

Designed as the lightest and most compact Kindle, it has a 300ppi high-res display screen, measuring 6 inches. It also has 16GB of storage space for housing thousands of your favourite e-books.

The Kindle Paperwhite standard model is a gorgeous upgrade to your ageing e-reader. With a glare-free display, seven weeks of battery, adjustable light and a waterproof rating, this Kindle can come with you anywhere.

The Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition doubles the storage of the standard model and features wireless charging. It is available in two shiny colourways: Metallic Jade and Metallic Black.

Now at an all-time low for Black Friday, this is a popular e-reader and one of the best colour models we've seen to date.

With 32GB storage, an auto-adjusting front light and a vibrant colour display, the Kindle Colorsoft Signature improves on the standard edition by adding wireless charging to the mix.

This iPad Air makes for a great laptop replacement, with 1TB of storage more than capable of housing all your work apps and games, too. The M4 chip gives it some serious power; it's Wi-Fi 7-enabled and comes with a USB-C port.

Score a tidy AU$1,000 off this iPad Pro and Apple Pencil Pro this Black Friday. With 2TB of storage space, Wi-Fi and Cellular capability, a nice 11-inch glass display and the superpower processor of the M5 chip, this tablet and pen duo will make a great laptop replacement and then some.

The cable provides a more reliable and stable connection to source devices, though a 3.5mm-to-USB or Lightning adapter will likely be required for phone compatibility. Once connected, they deliver exceptional high-fidelity sound. As expected from Sennheiser, they feature outstanding build quality and offer exceptional comfort for extended listening sessions.

Hey runners, if you're serious about your sport, you may want to consider the Shokz OpenRun Pro 2. These open-ear headphones are built for performance, delivering better bass and a super secure, comfy fit for those long runs. Plus, you can take calls clearly, and the open-ear design means you'll always be aware of what's happening around you.

If swimming is more your thing, the Shokz OpenSwim Pro 2 are excellent for listening to tunes while doing laps. Apart from being IP68 water resistant, they offer 9 hours of listening time and 32GB of storage for MP3s. And thanks to Bluetooth 5.4 connectivity, they're just as good for running.

Available in a fair few colourways at this fantastic discount, the JBL Charge 5 can bring the party, and quite loudly, I might add. I use this Bluetooth speaker at home myself and love it, with up to 20 hours of playback. It's also dust and waterproof (IP67 rating), so you can take it anywhere, plus it will double as a phone charger in a pinch if you need some extra juice on your handset.

The Bose Ultra Open Earbuds deliver the power and quality you’d expect from Bose, with the added perks of an open-ear design. The immersive sound is top-notch, offering up to seven hours of playtime and as much as 48 hours on standby. They’re reliable, effortless, and perform beautifully. This discount is available in a few colours under the same listing.

Okay, so it's not the most mind-blowing deal we've ever seen, but even a 21% discount on Apple's awesome AirPods Max 2 is definitely worth a look. Now down by AU$211.

Amazon's offering the biggest discount on Apple's third-gen AirPods Pro earphones we've seen to date. Though some of the improvements over their forebears are small, these are still indisputably the best in-ear AirPods ever, with better noise cancellation, fuller bass and crisper treble, plus smart features like live language translation and heart rate monitoring.

The Sennheiser Accentum Wireless cans offer clean sound, even if they aren't as dynamic-sounding as Sennheiser's Momentum headphones, but they do offer impressive ANC and a long 50-hour battery life. Now 51% off, this is the second-lowest price we've seen on these great over-ear cans.

Love the thrill of a blind box keyring? The Kodak Charmera is worth getting your hands on. We gave it 4 stars in our review, as it is, simply put, "cute, cheap and lo-fi". You're not going to get high-definition quality out of it, but you'll get a cute keyring camera with vintage aesthetic photos and videos. The Charmera has 11 different filters and frames to choose from, and comes with a USB-C cord for easy charging. You'll only need to add a microSD card with a GB capacity of your choice to transfer your pics. Oh, and your selected colourway? That's anyone's guess, as the Charmera comes in seven mystery colours, including a "secret" rare option.

Capturing 4K content just got cuter with this tiny Insta360 Go 3S camera. It's totally magnetic, so you can stick it to most surfaces and capture 360-degree POVs. With 25% off on Amazon, this bundle is great for budding content creators, adventurers, and risk-takers on the go.

We gave this fully automatic machine a 3-star rating, as we found it was rather ambitious and some of its results were mediocre, but our reviewer said it was relatively easy to use. With a nice saving, it's hard to dismiss this Breville coffee machine deal. The Barista Express has a built-in grinder, tamper, and bean hopper, so there's no need to buy a separate grinder or hand tamp. Available in a few colourways under the same listing.

Equipped with a steam wand, controlled dosage and grind settings and active temperature control, the De'Longhi La Specialista Arte is the perfect beginner-friendly manual machine. It's also compact, meaning it won't take up much bench space, and comes with everything you need to make your perfect brew on the first go. Now discounted by 23%, this is the perfect Black Friday purchase if you're a lover of all things caffeine.

Just AU$1 more than its lowest price ever of AU$87, this Nespresso Vertuo Pop machine is hard to pass up at a massive 62% off in the Solo White colourway. With one-touch convenience, you can brew up to four different cup sizes from a range of great Nespresso coffee pods. You'll also receive a 12-pack of coffee capsule samples to try.

Now at its lowest price in the last month, you can't surpass the one-touch convenience of a Nespresso Vertuo Pop. Now available in this Coconut White colourway on Amazon, with a complimentary coffee pod sample kit and milk frother.

The Creatista is also an excellent performer, capable of brewing your morning coffee exceptionally fast. Do note, this price was AU$100 cheaper yesterday, so it might fluctuate throughout today.

As an iced coffee all-year-round enjoyer, the Ninja Luxe Cafe has changed my life, thanks to its cold-pressed espresso presets and its specialty Dual Froth system with a cold-foam setting.

The kit comes with two detachable probes, an LCD screen displaying temperature and a charging cord. Interested in adding a multicooker to your kitchen's arsenal? This one from Ninja can pressure cook, steam, slow cook, sear, bake, roast and more, so you can prepare meals in one compact device. Now 55% off.

Ninja's original glass air fryer packs 1700W of power into a portable design, with two borosilicate glass containers that serve as both frying baskets and serving dishes. The borosilicate means they can also withstand extreme temperatures, making it easy to take your favourite foods from frozen to crispy. The Crispi also comes with two removable crisping grates and two snap-on container lids for easy food storage post-feast.

Want an air fryer and induction cooker all-in-one? Meet Tefal's YumMeal. You can prep, cook, eat and clean in the same bowl, making it perfect for smaller households with minimal storage space.

Tefal's SuperGrill is the answer to all your cooking and grilling needs at home. It can act like an indoor barbecue, grilling your favourite proteins, and it can toast, broil and melt. Now discounted by 50%, if you're looking for a 3-in-1 grill plate, Tefal's SuperGrill is one to consider.

Designed to spot messes the naked eye can miss, the Shark PowerDetect UV Reveal uses light to detect hidden stains and spills on your hard floors. Better yet, it also features a heated mop that can scrub the toughest stains. It's also equipped with LiDAR navigation, an anti-tangle roller brush, eight PowerDetect modes that adapt to your flooring and a NeverTouch Pro Base that handles the debris and self-cleaning for you.

Nab one of Dyson's most impressive cordless vacs and a car cleaning kit for less this Black Friday. Now 62% off, the V8 Advanced is the perfect runaround cordless vacuum for budget-minded Dyson fans, and it doesn't hurt that this price includes three more handheld attachments to get into all the nooks and crannies of your home and car.

This Ecovacs Deebot T30s Pro deal shouldn't be swept away. With powerful suction, smart mopping features, anti-tangle technology, and a self-cleaning auto-empty station, the T30s Pro can handle messes on both carpets and hard floors, making it an ideal spring cleaning companion.

If you're after something a little more automated to help you maintain a dust-free living space every day, this Ecovacs could be a top contender. The Dreame H15 Pro Heat is a sleek, competent wet/dry vacuum excelling on hard floors. The heated wash mode offers effective cleaning and shiny floors. There's also decent dry cleaning on hard floors.

You'll never have to worry about any wet (or pet) messes at home ever again with the Shark StainStriker. This powerful spot cleaner gets rid of tough stains and spots in a breeze, so much so that you might not even realise there was a mess in the first place.

While we haven't reviewed this particular model, we gave its predecessor, the Shark HydroVac, a massive 4.5 stars in our review, as it proved to be a powerful tool for grime and dirt on both hard and carpeted floors. In the market for a wet-dry vac? This Roborock is one to consider. With a blue light to help find hidden debris, 22,000Pa suction power and steam functionality, this Roborock is perfect for every kind of wet (or dry) messes.

The Shark NeverChange purifier with a HEPA-certified filter that traps airborne allergens and pollutants; this purifier will ensure you breathe easily and clean deeply, no matter what floats through your home.

Calling all pet owners, parents, and messy eaters, this little machine is for you. Using warm water and stain formula, this carpet washer quickly removes spots and stains from carpets, furniture, rugs and more, with ease. Saving you time and money, this machine is worth every penny.

While the Saucony Triumph 23 is not the most exciting running shoe, it has a couple of key features to recommend it. One is that it's very comfortable and protective, and the other is its durability. That said, it's now discounted by up to 44% in both men's and women's sizes, which is one of the deepest discounts we've seen, so it could be worth nabbing ASAP.

Knocking up to 50% off, these Crocs Classic clogs are extremely versatile, breathable and dry fast when wet, making them perfect for almost every activity. Available in a range of colours under the same listing — and note that some colourways are a little pricier than others.

These Crocs Toe Loop sandals are ideal for summer, providing both style and comfort. Available in a range of sizes and colours under the same listing.

Never heard of Heydude shoes? Well, let me introduce them to you. This Wally style comes with great (and comfy) features, including a flexible outsole, removable insole and stretchy canvas upper.

These Heydude comfy stretch canvas boat-style shoes are totally hands-free, so you can slide them on while you're halfway out the door. They're flexible, lightweight and have a removable insole.

Can't sleep without the dull sound of white noise in the background? You're not alone. If you can't afford a Hatch alarm clock, then this Glocusent is one to consider. It does all the same things — plays white noise, has a dimmable light and smart display — but comes at a fraction of the price. Now discounted to AU$62.99 for Black Friday.

Hitting fitness goals can be tricky, and it always helps to have the right tools in your arsenal to get you there faster. The Homebuds Digital Scales provide accurate results every time, thanks to the in-built auto calibration and weight sensors. The scales come with batteries included and a bright LED screen for displaying results.

Need a new emotional support water bottle? Try this Owala. With insulated stainless steel, it'll keep any of your favourite cold beverages cool for hours at a time, and you can customise your colourway from the various vivid options under the same listing.

Is a tumbler more your speed? Then perhaps you could be persuaded by this style from Owala as well. Complete with an easy-to-carry side handle and spout/straw lid, this tumbler can go everywhere with you.

As a cat mum, I've been using a PetSafe ScoopFree litter box for a few years now, and it's changed my life. Never did I ever think I'd enjoy sucking "gunk" out of my face on a Friday evening, but now it's become a crucial part of my weekly routine. An even cheaper alternative in the hairdryer space is the Dreame Gleam. It has a speedy 110,000 RPM motor, customisable settings and built-in ion technology for a frizz-free finish every time.

Shark's latest airstyler, the Glam, is a notable improvement on the Flexstyle, incorporating new styling attachments to make it a 4-in-1 styler. You'll need to act fast to grab this 5-star rated styler, as it's sure to sell out at this discounted rate!

If you need a new hairdryer, but don't require all the bells and whistles of a Dyson Supersonic or Shark Speedstyle, then this Remington Aero 2000 is a great option. This stunning 6,020-piece Lego Harry Potter Hogwarts Castle set, including 4 minifigures, gives fans a glimpse into the microscale world of Harry Potter — but beware of the Basilisk! With hours of interactive play, muggles will be spellbound with this enchanting set.

Looking for a challenge? Take the Lego Vincent Van Gogh three-dimensional Starry Night recreation for a spin. This kit includes a massive amount of bricks; more than 2,300!

Who knew a Lego Botanicals set could be this adorable? These Lego dracaena and pilae plants come in pots with faces, arms and legs. They're perfect for adding cuteness and colour to your home decor.

After a fun Lego set to brighten your home decor? This gorgeous rose bouquet made of Lego is the perfect addition to any space and will give you plenty of time to relax while making the 4-piece set. Plus, this set would make the perfect anniversary gift or present for a loved one.

If you don't need a luggage set, but need a bigger suitcase to lug your purchases around when you're overseas, might I suggest this 82cm bag from American Tourister. Now 53% off at Amazon, this Light Max case has double compartments, an expandable zip and is extremely lightweight, making it a dream to push around.

The Amazon Black Friday sale starts ten days earlier than the sales event, kicking off on November 17, 2026 and ending at 11:59pm AEDT on November 30, 2026.

This year's Amazon Black Friday deals period begins on Tuesday, November 17 in Australia and then wraps up after Cyber Monday, November 30. That's a full fortnight of deals and discounts on Amazon AU.

If you spot a great Black Friday deal on Amazon, there's still a chance that it may end up being even cheaper as the sale progresses. That said, the online retailer doesn't always keep the same deals going for the entire Black Friday sales period, and stock doesn't always last, so buying early might be worth considering if you want to avoid disappointment.

#3123. Noodles: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors

Ramen is now a permanent menu category, giving Noodles a steady sales base that seasonal flavor rotations can build on.

By The Motley Fool Team – Nov 26, 2026 at 1:38PM EST

10 stocks we like better than Noodles & Co ›

On its third quarter of 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 13, 2026, Noodles (NDLS -2.61%) announced systemwide comparable restaurant sales growth of 9.5%, driven by customer traffic gains and store portfolio changes. For long-term investors, the chain's ability to boost sales while shrinking store count points to efficiency gains, though sustaining them is the test. Three key takeaways from management stand out.

Closing underperforming locations not only trimmed overhead from the restaurant network. Nearby locations captured off-premise orders from shuttered units, lifting average restaurant volume across the remaining footprint.

Management expanded its menu by making ramen a permanent offering to drive traffic. The category gives the chain a predictable sales base while allowing seasonal flavor rotations throughout the year.

Average unit volume, or AUV--the average annual sales generated per location--jumped over 15% to $1.54 million during the quarter. Higher volumes expanded restaurant-level contribution margin to 16.7% by leveraging fixed expenses across a leaner footprint.

Sales momentum continues as store efficiencies take hold. Higher unit volumes and disciplined cost controls support margin expansion while management tracks traffic trends.

A leaner restaurant footprint and lower debt strengthen financial flexibility entering 2027. Long-term value relies on sustaining customer traffic through continuous menu innovation.

#3122. Top Wall Street analysts are upbeat about the prospects for these 3 stocks

September ended on a mixed note, with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average falling 0.5% and 4.3%, respectively, while the Nasdaq Composite climbed 1.9%. Markets remained on edge with higher oil prices and Treasury yields weighing on investor sentiment and triggering fears of additional interest rate hikes.

In this climate, investors with a long-term horizon can track recommendations from top Wall Street analysts to find stocks with solid growth prospects.

Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Neocloud company CoreWeave (CRWV) is benefiting from robust AI-driven demand for cloud computing.

Recently, JPMorgan analyst Samik Chatterjee upgraded CoreWeave to buy from hold, raising his price target to $125 from $120. The analyst cited favorable pricing, driven by solid demand, for the upgrade.

Chatterjee said CoreWeave is now more willing to sign premium priced, shorter-term contracts, which lift his revenue and margin estimates. CRWV stock performance has been underwhelming as investors worry about high capital spending, the analyst noted. That said, he believes that higher prices and increased margins will more than offset the rise in debt to fund capital spending, improving the stock's valuation.

Chatterjee noted the 25% price hike in July across CoreWeave's product offerings and frequent price increases by rivals like Nebius (NBIS), adding that some peers are charging nearly three times more for short-term compute contracts than what CoreWeave charges on longer-term deals.

"CoreWeave's leverage of the opportunity [is] evident in its recent press release highlighting contracts signed in F3Q at ~$40M/MW," said Chatterjee. JPMorgan said higher pricing is already contributing 5-10 percentage points to contract margins versus earlier deals.

Chatterjee ranks No. 4 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 75% of the time, delivering an average return of 55.3%. See CoreWeave Statistics on TipRanks.

Palo Alto Networks (PANW) is a provider of cybersecurity solutions across network, cloud, security operations, AI and identity. Following a discussion with management, BTIG analyst Gray Powell reiterated a buy rating on PANW and raised his price target to $425 from $404.

After a review of Palo Alto's product-level growth catalysts, Powell sees clear upside to both revenue and next-generation security (NGS) annual recurring revenue (ARR) in fiscal 2027. He expects PANW to deliver pro forma revenue growth of more than 17%, above the consensus estimate of 14.6%, and NGS ARR growth of more than 26% versus the Street's expectation of 24.5%.

Over the past five years, the Palo Alto business mix, has moved to higher-growth product areas and new markets. from what was earlier viewed as a hardware-centric network security company, Powell said. The 5-star analyst estimates that hardware firewalls and attached subscriptions now account for less than 50% of revenue.

Meanwhile, high-growth solutions, including Prisma SASE, software firewalls, Cortex XSIAM, Chronosphere and Idira now represent more than 35% of PANW's revenue. "Investors may not fully realize the growth potential within PANW's platform story," Powell said.

BTIG is optimistic about the prospects of Chronosphere in observability, CyberArk in identity and software firewalls and Prisma AIRS in the network and AI security business.

Powell ranks No. 320 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 61% of the time, delivering an average return of 17.3%. See Palo Alto Networks KPIs on TipRanks.

In a research note on September 30, Rosenblatt analyst Scott Devitt reiterated a buy rating on e-commerce and cloud computing platform Amazon (AMZN), raising his price target to $360 from $335. Fears that agentic commerce poses a major threat to Amazon's advertising business seem "overstated," he said.

Devitt noted that the growing adoption of personal agents and AI shopping assistants has sparked concern about displacement of Amazon's retail media business. But the 5-star analyst remains bullish, given Amazon's ability to adapt to changing consumer behavior, as it's done in the past.

Additionally, Devitt argues that even if an AI agent helps a shopper discover a product, Amazon can still handle the purchase and delivery, keeping much of the transaction value. He highlighted that management believes that existing Amazon shoppers will likely continue to start their shopping journey on the platform because it has better personalization, accurate pricing and inventory information that third-party agents still lack.

Overall, Devitt expects Amazon's retail business to prove a net beneficiary of agentic commerce. Fewer clicks would not hurt the company if the value of each remaining click and overall volumes keep rising, he said. The argument is that even if Amazon loses some sponsored ad revenue over the next few years, it would likely be only a small part of the company's total business and could be offset by growth in other areas.

"Consistent with our AI framework, we continue to view Amazon as one of the most resilient leaders in our coverage, combining owned compute infrastructure with a physical fulfillment moat," said Devitt. His bullish view is supported, Devitt said, by expectations that Amazon Web Services (AWS) will exit the year at a more than 45% growth rate with continued margin improvement.

Devitt ranks No. 765 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 49% of the time, delivering an average return of 12%. See Amazon Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

#3121. MacBook Neo vs MacBook Air: Which should you buy right now?

Apple’s Mac lineup is stronger than ever this year, largely thanks to the new MacBook Neo. If you’re deciding between the MacBook Neo and the MacBook Air this holiday season, here’s everything you need to know.

The MacBook Neo is Apple’s most affordable laptop ever, starting at $699 (currently on sale for $599). It features a solid aluminum design that comes in a range of fun colors, including Silver, Blush, Citrus, and Indigo

Unlike Apple’s other Macs, the MacBook Neo is powered by an A-series chip rather than an M-series chip. It uses the A18 Pro chip originally introduced with the iPhone 16 Pro, featuring a 6-core CPU and 5-core GPU.

The MacBook Neo comes with 8GB of unified memory, with no additional RAM configuration options available. It starts with 256GB of storage, with a 512GB configuration available for an additional $100. That $100 upgrade also gets you Touch ID, which is not included in the base model.

There are some other trade-offs compared to the MacBook Air. The MacBook Neo lacks a backlit keyboard, MagSafe charging, and a Force Touch trackpad. It also has more limited USB-C connectivity and supports just one external display.

Still, the MacBook Neo offers an impressive feature set. It has a 13-inch display, up to 16 hours of battery life, a 1080p FaceTime camera, and the full macOS experience.

The MacBook Air, meanwhile, was updated earlier this year with Apple’s M5 chip. It starts at $1,299, making it $600 more expensive than the entry-level MacBook Air. The MacBook Air is currently on sale with a starting price of $999.

For that $600 upgrade, the MacBook Air offers several key advantages over the MacBook Air. The M5 chip has a 10-core CPU and up to a 10-core GPU, enabling better sustained performance than the MacBook Neo.

The MacBook Air also starts with 16GB of unified memory and 512GB of storage, both double the entry-level MacBook Neo. You can configure it with up to 32GB of memory and 4TB of storage, while the MacBook Neo is limited to 8GB of memory and 512GB of storage.

Apple rates the MacBook Air for up to 18 hours of video streaming and 15 hours of wireless web browsing, compared to 16 hours and 11 hours, respectively, for the MacBook Neo.

As I wrote in my review earlier this year, I think the MacBook Neo is a great Mac, full stop … not just because of the great price. It can handle the vast majority of things most people will throw at it. This includes web browsing, basic photo and video editing, research, and much more.

The M5 MacBook Air, meanwhile, offers more power and more configuration options. This makes it a great option for people who need more storage, RAM, and power than the MacBook Neo can offer.

One of my favorite things about the MacBook Air is that it’s available in two screen sizes. The 15-inch MacBook Air is one of my favorite Apple laptops with a combination of the ultra-thin and light design and the larger screen. I think a lot of people forget it exists, but it’s an excellent choice.

To recap, I think the MacBook Neo is a great choice for everyday tasks like web browsing, email, writing, and streaming. The MacBook Air is a better fit for more demanding workflows, including photo and video editing, coding, working with large spreadsheets, and heavy multitasking.

Beyond performance, the MacBook Air offers a handful of niceties that you won’t find on the MacBook Neo. These include a backlit keyboard, a larger display with True Tone, MagSafe charging, a better webcam and speakers, and a Force Touch trackpad. It also includes Touch ID on every configuration, longer battery life, and support for two external displays.

If it’s in the budget, I think the MacBook Air is an excellent choice for all Mac shoppers. It’s plenty powerful, thin and light, and is highly configurable compared to the MacBook Neo.

What do you think of the MacBook Neo vs MacBook Air decision? Which would you choose? Let us know down in the comments.

Terrestrial networks cannot reach every location. Oceans, remote regions, and disaster zones often remain without coverage. 5G non-terrestrial networks (NTN) address this gap by using satellites and high-altitude platforms. Introduced in 3GPP Release 17, NR-NTN keeps evolving through Releases 18, 19, and 20. Satellite links bring new challenges. Signals travel long distances, satellites move at high speed, and Doppler shift affects synchronization and timing. These effects shape payload design, mobility procedures, and device behavior. They also call for new testing methods for devices, satellites, and networks. This paper explains the technology step by step. It also shows how NTN is shaping unified terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks in 6G.

#3116. iOS 28 to ‘revamp’ iPhone notifications, per report

iOS 28 is coming next year, and a new rumor says the update will “revamp the iPhone’s notification system.” This comes as Android has introduced features like “Notification Organizer” to help users sort notifications into different categories.

9to5Mac is sponsored by Sony: Score Sony’s INZONE noise-canceling earbuds for 38% off. These deliver immersive 360 Spatial Sound, active noise canceling, low-latency wireless connectivity, and much more.

The report cites “multiple sources” and comes from MacRumors. There aren’t any specific details about what changes iOS 28 will introduce for notifications. “The sources said iOS 28 will include significant changes to Notification Center, but we do not have any specific details,” the report says.

The iOS notifications system is overdue for an update. While Apple has added features like Apple Intelligence-based priority notifications and notification summaries, the system still lacks other organization and sorting settings.

Android 16 introduced several significant notification changes, focused primarily on reducing clutter and prioritizing important information. For Pixel devices, the update also introduced Notification Organizer, a feature that automatically groups and silences low-priority alerts, including promotions, news, and social media notifications.

As Abner explained on 9to5Google last year:

The Notification Organizer will sort your alerts into the following categories: Promotions, News, Social, and Suggested. The first two are already on, but you must enable the remaining ones. There’s also an option to “Always expand bundles.”

I’d love for Apple to adopt a similar system on iPhone, iPad, and Mac. Even with the recent Apple Intelligence additions, the iOS notifications system is still far too basic.

What changes do you think Apple should make to notifications with iOS 28? Do you use features like priority notifications and notification summaries? Let us know down in the comments.

The SweetNight is a great cooling mattress for under $400 in a queen size. I slept on it for over three weeks and recommend it to back and stomach sleepers looking for a good all-rounder that's breathable, supportive, and has strong edge support.

Under $350 for a queen, the EgoHome Black 12" is another solid choice for combination. sleepers. We'd question whether there's enough support for people who weigh over 300lbs, but are confident when recommending this to most other sleepers.

A 30% off sale takes the 10" Brooklyn Bedding CopperFlex Essential below $500 for a queen. Super cushioning, it's plusher than the Sweetnight, making it ideal for side sleepers who weigh under 150lbs and who enjoy soft mattresses.

This month, I retested the EGOHOME Black mattress, a memory foam bed with a budget-friendly price tag, and I was pleased to discover that it still delivers side sleeper comfort and excellent value for money. But this year, I've also rigorously tested two other impressive all-foam: the SweetNight CoolNest and the CopperFlex Essential.

Like many of the beds found in this year's best mattress guide, a memory foam mattress should feature foam layers that delivers body-cradling comfort — and these three affordable options offered me just that during testing. However, while the mattresses are all ideal for side sleeping, there are key differences between them.

In this Sweetnight CoolNest vs EGOHOME Black vs CopperFlex Essential comparison guide, I'll draw on my own experience of lab testing and sleeping on each mattress to explore the differences in price, designs, and comfort. That way, you can make an informed decision when you're looking for a mattress under $500 for a queen in this month's Black Friday mattress sales.

All three of these mattresses are under $500 in a queen this Black Friday, with the EGOHOME and SweetNight always coming in at less than $400 in a queen (which puts them in the budget price tier). Meanwhile, the price of a queen CopperFlex Essential is between $400 and $600, depending on what sale is on. Either way, the CopperFlex is a mid-range bed.

You don't need to be super strategic about when you buy yourself a SweetNight CoolNest, as a queen is pretty much always $399.99 (I've yet to see it on sale for a different price). However, if you time your purchase right, you can often snag two free pillows (worth $100) with your CoolNest bed. We saw this deal during the Labor Day mattress sales, and I'm hoping it may return as Black Friday draws closer.

The EGOHOME is the cheapest of the bunch, and is now $379 for a queen (MSRP is $559, but it's always on sale). However, during holiday sales, you can generally enter a promo code at checkout to knock an extra 10% off the sale price. This is the case right now, with the promo code PREVIEW10 taking a queen down to $341.10.

The Brooklyn Bedding mattress sale oscillates between 25% off and 30% off, with the former being a standard discount and the latter being the deal that's trotted out during big events and holidays like the current Black Friday sale. Basically, if you see 30% off at Brooklyn Bedding, you know you're getting the top deal. With the current 30% discount, a queen CopperFlex Essential is now $489.30 (it's over $500 during the 25% off sales).

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

As for extras, the CopperFlex Essential boasts the most generous benefits: a year-long sleep trial, a lifetime warranty, and free shipping. EGOHOME and SweetNight also provide free shipping, but their trials and warranties are slightly shorter. However, that's not a complaint — a 10-year warranty and a 100-night sleep trial are perfectly sufficient.

The 12" CoolNest Memory Foam Mattress is $399.99 in a queen right now, which isn't anything new. However, there is a chance that you may snag some freebies as we get closer to Black Friday, as we saw free pillows during Labor Day. Whenever you buy, though, expect a 10-year warranty and 100-night sleep trial.

With the EGOHOME code PREVIEW 10, you can take a queen size EGOHOME Black 12" Foam mattress from $379 (MSRP:$559) down to $341.10. This is excellent value for money, and you can also receive a 10-year warranty and a 100-night sleep trial.

Brooklyn Bedding has ditched its standard 25% discount for Black Friday and rolled out its big 30% off sale. This dunks a queen size CopperFlex Essential under $500, with a queen now $489.30. Thanks to a huge shakeup to 3Z brand's mattress extras, the CopperFlex now comes with a lifetime warranty and one-year trial.

Like the best memory foam mattresses on the market, all three beds are made entirely of foam (not a spring nor coil in sight) and are fiberglass-free.

The 12" SweetNight's design is focused on cooling, with an airflow-enhancing '3D' cover that my fellow testers and I found to be extremely cool-to-the-touch (but more on that later). Its foam is also infused with Phase Change Material (PCM), a specialist cooling fabric found in some of the best cooling mattresses. PCM has been proven to improve human heat dissipation up to 25.6% compared to conventional mattresses

The 12" EGOHOME does have a graphene-infused cover that the brand calls "cooling", but this is very basic. That said, the EGOHOME has an excellent quality build, packed with dense layers of foam (including a EGOHOME's trademarked BraceSleeper Support Foam, which is high-density for extra durability).

Despite being mid-range rather than budget, the CopperFlex has the least sophisticated design out of the three mattresses, with just a copper-infused foam for temperature control. However, its cover does boast a "Nano Stain Terminator Protector" cover to safeguards against stains and spills, plus it comes in a wide range of sizes (including an Olympic queen and RV sizes).

I found all three beds to be good choices for anyone seeking the best mattress for side sleepers (and I say that as a primary side sleeper), but each did boast different levels of pressure relief.

In my SweetNight CoolNest mattress review, I found that the CoolNest provided excellent pressure relief for side and back sleeping (both in objective and subjective tests). It has enough give in the shoulder and hip region to relieve the side-sleeper pressure points, but its ultra-quick response time means it's easy to move around on and avoids that "quicksand" feel that some memory foam mattresses have.

I conducted the EGOHOME Black 12" Foam mattress review for seven months (the longest I've tested a mattress at home) and found it delivered excellent medium-firm support for all sleep positions. However, another tester (a stomach sleeper) considered it a little too soft for front sleeping, proving that mattress firmness is subjective. That said, back and side sleepers should feel both comfortable and supported.

As for the CopperFlex Essential, it's clear from our tests that it's strictly for side sleepers. I found it incredibly cushioning when sleeping on it for my Brooklyn Bedding CopperFlex Essential mattress review, which is surprising as it doesn't have a pillow top. It scored the highest pressure relief score out of the three mattresses, but my fellow testers and I agreed that it's too plush for stomach sleeping.

From the moment I unboxed the SweetNight CoolNest, I found it to be incredibly cool to the touch. I even slept on it through summer heatwaves without AC and it still delivered optimal temperature regulation. My experience was backed up by our thermal imaging camera tests, which found that the SweetNight has a rapid cooling rate of 2.1°F per minute (a cooling rate even quicker than the Bear Elite's 1.82°F per minute).

In contrast, I found that both the CopperFlex Essential and the EGOHOME Black retained heat, especially in the back and shoulder region. Out of the three mattresses, the EGOHOME absorbed the highest amount of heat (15.6°F ), which was definitely noticeable to both me and fellow tester, Ruth Jones. And while the CopperFlex Essential absorbed up to 11.1°F in comparison, its temperature control will pose a problem for hot sleepers.

✅ You want cooler nights: The SweetNight boasts a cool-to-the-touch cover and heat-dissipating PCM which provides a cooler sleep even during hot weather.

✅ You sleep on your side or back: Its medium-firm foam is soft enough to soothe side sleepers but supportive enough for back sleepers. Plus, it's responsive enough for you to change position without feeling 'stuck' in the foam.

✅ You want the best value for money: The EGOHOME Black 12" Foam is the cheapest option, with promo codes adding extra discount to already cheap sale prices.

✅ You're a combination sleeper: I found it to be supportive in all sleep positions, and the medium-firm feel is ideal for side and back sleeping.

✅ You want the most cushioning: Its plush pressure relief is ideal for dedicated side sleepers, even if it's not such a great choice for back and stomach sleepers.

✅ You want generous extras: With a lifetime warranty and a trial that lasts a full year, the CopperFlex boasts the best benefits.

Frances Daniels is a PPA-accredited journalist and Sleep Staff Writer at Tom's Guide with an MA in Magazine Journalism from Cardiff University. Her role includes covering mattress and sleep news and writing sleep product reviews and buyer's guides, including our Best Hybrid Mattress 2025 guide. She is interested in the relationship between sleep and health, interviewing an array of experts to create in-depth articles about topics such as nutrition, sleep disorders, sleep hygiene, and mattress care. She is also our specialist on mattress toppers — producing bed topper reviews and taking care of our Best Mattress Toppers 2025 guide — and leads content relating to fiberglass-free beds for a non-toxic sleep. Outside of Tom's Guide, she has written for Ideal Home and Marie Claire.

#3113. PDD: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors

Shifting spend from traffic subsidies into rural delivery networks is a bet on reach, not just cheaper prices.

By The Motley Fool Team – Nov 26, 2026 at 2:01PM EST

10 stocks we like better than PDD Holdings ›

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 19, 2026, PDD (PDD +0.23%) announced that it is expanding support for merchants beyond platform operations directly into manufacturing and supply chain infrastructure. For long-term investors, this strategic pivot from short-term marketing spend to deep infrastructure upgrades shows management's focus on building durable operational moats. Strengthening supply chain capabilities directly protects merchant retention and customer loyalty against lower-cost rivals. Three takeaways from management's call stand out.

PDD is shifting resources away from basic traffic subsidies to fund research and development (R&D), manufacturing, and fulfillment capabilities across industrial clusters. Partnering directly with factories allows merchants to establish proprietary brands and improve operational efficiency.

PDD is expanding its free-shipping-to-villages initiative to address last-mile delivery bottlenecks in remote agricultural regions. Covering transport costs from county transit hubs to rural pickup points opens untapped consumer demand and drives merchant order volume.

Management remains focused on strategic investments under its 100 Billion Support Program rather than quarterly expense ratios. PDD prioritizes long-term supply chain resilience over short-term marketing campaigns to maintain consumer trust and platform competitiveness.

Domestic e-commerce competition remains fierce as buyers evaluate prices across platforms. PDD is strengthening supply chain infrastructure, rural fulfillment, and merchant governance to protect market share.

Evolving overseas trade policies create friction for cross-border sellers. Management is expanding warehouse partnerships and local fulfillment infrastructure to build supply chain resilience.
